---
title: "Sign-up Email Code Speed"
description: "How fast sign-up email codes are entered: codes entered and the median seconds per day."
---

How quickly people enter the code CanadaLogin emails them during sign-up, as the
median seconds from the code being sent to it being entered, per day.

A person has to open their inbox, find the message, and type the code, which
takes a while. A bot reading the mailbox programmatically does it in a few
seconds, so a day whose median drops sharply is a sign of automated sign-ups.
This is a detection signal: the Automated Traffic dashboard holds the thresholds
that turn it into a flag.

It reads the [raw event stream](../../catalog/ibm_verify_events_raw/mfa_activity.qmd),
because the summary table has no timestamps.

## Calculation

Take `Email OTP` events from the sign-up client (`performedby_type = 'api'`).
Link each code to its entry through the hashed email address, `mfadevice`, leaving
out a blank or `UNKNOWN` one: order each address's events by time, and keep a
`success` whose previous event was a `sent`. That pairs an entry with the code
sent just before it, and drops a success after a failure, which would otherwise
time the retry rather than the code.

The time to enter is the seconds between the two, rounded down and capped at 600,
so one code left overnight cannot drag a day's figures. Report each ET day's codes
entered and the median of their times. The median is the lower median: the
smallest time with at least half the day's codes at or below it.

Filter on the UTC `year`, `month`, and `day` partitions, and read one UTC day
either side of the window: an ET day ends at 04:00 or 05:00 UTC the next day, and
a code entered early in the window may have been sent the day before. Times are
whole seconds, so a code sent and entered in the same second tie; order by
`result` as well, which puts `sent` first.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

```sql
WITH events AS (
    SELECT
        mfadevice,
        result,
        from_iso8601_timestamp(replace(substr(time, 1, 19), ' ', 'T') || 'Z') AS at
    FROM ibm_verify_events_raw.mfa_activity
    -- UTC partitions: the window, plus one day either side
    WHERE year = '2026'
      AND (month = '09' OR (month = '08' AND day = '31') OR (month = '10' AND day = '01'))
      AND mfamethod = 'Email OTP'
      -- the sign-up client
      AND performedby_type = 'api'
      AND mfadevice NOT IN ('', 'UNKNOWN', 'Unknown')
),
paired AS (
    SELECT
        result,
        at,
        -- result breaks a tie within one second: "sent" sorts before "success"
        lag(result) OVER (PARTITION BY mfadevice ORDER BY at, result) AS prev_result,
        lag(at) OVER (PARTITION BY mfadevice ORDER BY at, result) AS prev_at
    FROM events
),
entries AS (
    SELECT
        date(at_timezone(at, 'America/Toronto')) AS day,
        -- whole seconds, capped so one late entry cannot skew the day
        least(floor(to_unixtime(at) - to_unixtime(prev_at)), 600) AS seconds
    FROM paired
    WHERE result = 'success' AND prev_result = 'sent'
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        day,
        seconds,
        count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY day) AS codes_entered,
        row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY day ORDER BY seconds) AS position
    FROM entries
)

SELECT
    day,
    max(codes_entered) AS codes_entered,
    -- the lower median: the first time at or past half the day's codes
    min(seconds) FILTER (WHERE position >= codes_entered / 2.0) AS median_seconds
FROM ranked
-- set the reporting window in ET days; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
WHERE day BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-01' AND DATE '2026-09-30'
GROUP BY day
ORDER BY day;
```

## R

```r
tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify_events_raw", "mfa_activity")) |>
  # UTC partitions: the window, plus one day either side
  filter(
    year == "2026",
    month == "09" | (month == "08" & day == "31") | (month == "10" & day == "01"),
    mfamethod == "Email OTP",
    # the sign-up client
    performedby_type == "api",
    !mfadevice %in% c("", "UNKNOWN", "Unknown")
  ) |>
  mutate(at = sql("from_iso8601_timestamp(replace(substr(time, 1, 19), ' ', 'T') || 'Z')")) |>
  group_by(mfadevice) |>
  # result breaks a tie within one second: "sent" sorts before "success"
  window_order(at, result) |>
  mutate(prev_result = lag(result), prev_at = lag(at)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(result == "success", prev_result == "sent") |>
  mutate(
    day = sql("date(at_timezone(at, 'America/Toronto'))"),
    # whole seconds, capped so one late entry cannot skew the day
    seconds = sql("least(floor(to_unixtime(at) - to_unixtime(prev_at)), 600)")
  ) |>
  group_by(day) |>
  # counted before ordering, so it is the day's total, not a running count
  mutate(codes_entered = n()) |>
  window_order(seconds) |>
  mutate(position = row_number()) |>
  # set the reporting window in ET days; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  filter(day >= as.Date("2026-09-01"), day <= as.Date("2026-09-30")) |>
  summarise(
    codes_entered = max(codes_entered, na.rm = TRUE),
    # the lower median: the first time at or past half the day's codes
    median_seconds = min(if_else(position >= codes_entered / 2, seconds, NA), na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(day)
```

:::

:::

## Interpretation notes

**Read the median next to the count.** A fast median on a day with few codes is
noise; a fast median on a day with many more codes than usual is the pattern bot
sign-ups leave. The cap means a median of 600 seconds says "10 minutes or more",
not exactly 10 minutes.

**Only first-try entries are timed.** A success after a failure is left out, so
someone who mistyped the code once does not count. That keeps the figure about
reading the email, not about typing.

**It is expensive for long windows.** The query reads the raw table. Keep the
partition filter to the months you need.

## Alternative names

- email OTP speed
- sign-up email code entry time
- time to enter the email code
- sign-up speed
